Gerontological researchers study aging processes and older populations. While age is central to the field, it is often not the most important variable in research design because chronological age alone doesn't explain variability in aging outcomes.  
Gender can influence aging experiences but is not universally the most important variable.  
Time of measurement reflects when data is collected and can capture period effects, but it is not the primary conceptual variable.  
Cohort (the group of people born at the same time) is often the most important because aging cannot be separated from cohort effects — different generations age differently due to unique historical, social, and environmental exposures.  
Thus, cohort allows researchers to disentangle age, period, and cohort effects, which is a fundamental issue in gerontology.
